summary: Iteration 7 (real-sample accuracy + hybrid Flash-draft/Pro-refine) VERIFIED in-pipeline but a CRITICAL frontend regression surfaced on the public URL. Backend accuracy pytest `/app/backend/tests/test_real_sample_accuracy.py` passes: engine='gemini-pro' on `tests/fixtures/real_sample.jpg` returns word=91.67% / char=91.10% in 56.77s wall-clock on localhost (threshold 85%/90%). Spread on the same real image: gemini-flash 92.54% / 92.65% in 46.03s, gemma requested → fell back to gemini-pro (response engine echoed 'gemini-pro', text numbers 93.86% / 95.45% in 72.36s — this is NOT pure gemma, it is the fallback). The hybrid plan is wired correctly (ENGINE_PLAN gemini-pro = Flash draft + Pro refine) and the response `engine` field echoes the REQUESTED engine id when the preferred engine succeeds, as spec'd. `prepare_vision_inputs` on the real sample produces exactly 10 bands (matches ~10 target). Full backend suite 38/38 green in 130s (test_lipiscan_api + test_ai_vision_ocr + test_engine_selection + test_ocr_accuracy_iter6 + test_real_sample_accuracy). Tesseract (ben+eng) and Lohit-Bengali font are present. Frontend (390x844 web preview): Settings shows 3 engines with correct testIDs and labels — 'Best accuracy' (settings-engine-gemini-pro, default radio selected), 'Fast' (settings-engine-gemini-flash), 'Gemma 4 (open model)' (settings-engine-gemma); clicking Flash then Pro writes '"gemini-flash"' then '"gemini-pro"' to localStorage['lipiscan.ocr_engine']. Gallery flow drives through: New Scan → gallery fallback → file-choose real_sample.jpg → quality sheet (Sharpness / Lighting / Text detected all green) → Extract Text → review screen shows the correct loading copy 'Reading your handwriting line by line, then proofreading it — this can take up to a minute.' BUT the extract POST then returns 502 at exactly 60.3s and the review screen shows 'Request failed' with a Retry button. Reproduced out-of-band: `curl POST https://docx-capture.preview.emergentagent.com/api/extract ... real_sample.jpg` returns Cloudflare 502 at exactly 60.000s for BOTH engine=gemini-pro AND engine=gemini-flash. The same request to http://localhost:8001/api/extract succeeds in 56-72s. Short/synthetic pages (which take 7-13s) are unaffected and the review-engine-hint 'Read by Gemini 3 Flash + 3.1 Pro proofread' therefore could not be verified on the real sample through the UI (it will only render after a successful extract). All other endpoints are fine via the public URL (/api/quality-check 1.1s / 200, /api/ 200, history / cleanup / append-docx / download all green in pytest).

critical.issue: Hard 60s upstream timeout at the ingress returns Cloudflare 502 for real-world dense handwriting photos. The hybrid Flash-draft (10 bands) + Pro-refine pipeline measures 56.77s on localhost for gemini-pro and 46s for gemini-flash on the real sample, but 10 parallel vision calls + 1 refine call via the public URL exceed 60s and are killed. The frontend uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (public ingress) so every real-sample extract from the UI fails with 'Request failed'. Backend pytest passes only because it hits localhost:8001 directly.

minor.issue: On the dense real sample, the Hugging Face gemma call fails (likely HF router timeout / provider error for google/gemma-4-31B-it on a 1.2MB image + 10 bands) and the fallback chain promotes gemini-pro, so the response echoes engine='gemini-pro'. This is spec-correct fallback behaviour (test_engine_selection confirms gemma works on simpler pages), but it means pure-gemma numbers on this photograph are not observable from /api/extract — the 93.86/95.45 figures above are gemini-pro output after fallback, not gemma.

ui_bugs.issue: On real handwriting photos the extract POST 502s at 60s (ingress timeout), rendering the generic 'Request failed' error screen (review-error / review-retry-button). Retry just hits the same wall. Users will perceive the whole 'Best accuracy' engine as broken on the exact kind of page the user asked us to tune for.

integration_issues.issue: End-to-end flow stalls at the Extract step for dense real photos because /api/extract exceeds the 60s ingress timeout. Quality sheet, loading copy, and settings persistence all work correctly up to that point.

action_items: CRITICAL: Bring the real-sample /api/extract wall-clock under the 60s ingress ceiling for the public URL. Options: (a) switch ENGINE_PLAN['gemini-pro'] refine to gemini-flash (would still echo 'gemini-pro' as spec allows and keep ~45s), (b) make refine optional once draft looks confident (skip when band count > 8 and draft length > N), (c) return the draft immediately and run refine as a background task returning via /api/extract-status/{id} polling, or (d) ask platform to raise the ingress proxy_read_timeout from 60s for /api/extract specifically. Without this fix every dense real-page extract from the UI will 502.

MINOR: Investigate why gemma (google/gemma-4-31B-it via HF router) fails on this specific 1.2MB image / 10 bands and falls back to gemini-pro — likely HF timeout or image-size limit. Either shrink the band crops before HF calls or lower max_dim for the gemma plan so pure-gemma numbers become observable in the comparison the review request asked for.

After the latency fix, re-run the gallery → quality → review walk-through to confirm review-engine-hint renders 'Read by Gemini 3 Flash + 3.1 Pro proofread' and Append button is reachable on the real sample.

Measured 56.77s localhost / >60s public — right at the ingress ceiling. Consider conditional refine or background execution.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Measured numbers on /app/backend/tests/fixtures/real_sample.jpg are persisted in /app/test_reports/pytest/iter7_accuracy.json. The CRITICAL blocker is a 60-second upstream timeout at the public ingress (reproducible with: `time curl -X POST https://docx-capture.preview.emergentagent.com/api/extract -F file=@/app/backend/tests/fixtures/real_sample.jpg -F engine=gemini-pro --max-time 180` → 502 at exactly 60.00s). Localhost (http://localhost:8001) does not have this limit. The backend pytest harness goes to localhost so it stays green; the frontend uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL which is the public ingress, so the UI 502s on this exact photo. ENGINE_PLAN, DEFAULT_ENGINE and the three engine ids (gemini-pro / gemini-flash / gemma, dash not space) must not be changed. Preprocessing bands count on this sample = 10 — verified via `python -c 'from server import prepare_vision_inputs; ...'`. Gemma on this specific photo falls back silently to gemini-pro; test_engine_selection.py still confirms gemma itself is reachable on simpler pages.
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE of the frontend 'Request failed' on real handwriting: the Kubernetes/Cloudflare ingress fronting EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL enforces a 60-second upstream read timeout. The iteration-7 hybrid pipeline for engine='gemini-pro' on a 10-band Bengali page takes 56.77s on the backend container and 60-80s end-to-end through the ingress (TLS + proxy overhead + request/response size). That pushes every real-sample /api/extract call past the 60s ceiling and the ingress returns a Cloudflare 502. REPRODUCTION: `time curl -X POST https://docx-capture.preview.emergentagent.com/api/extract -F file=@/app/backend/tests/fixtures/real_sample.jpg -F engine=gemini-pro` → status 502 at 60.3s (gemini-flash: 502 at 60.3s as well). Same payload via localhost:8001 → 200 OK, word 91.67% / char 91.10%. MITIGATION: lower the extract wall-clock below ~45s for a dense page (skip refine when draft looks stable, or move refine to a background task + polling endpoint) OR raise the ingress proxy_read_timeout for /api/extract. The accuracy requirements are already met; it is purely a latency-vs-ingress-budget problem.
